packs.title: Stages, Stories and Gardens
packs.promise: Explore Nashville through its music landmarks, art, river views and gardens.

q.s: Learn one connection through the museum’s interpretation.
st: Choose an open gallery and read or listen to its interpretation.
Record a named musician and one stated connection to a musical tradition or another artist.
Credit the museum and add a question for later listening.

q.s: Notice the street’s visual rhythm at your own pace.
st: Choose a daylight public sidewalk position clear of queues.
Find three different exterior shapes or colors on building fronts.
Record a contrast without photographing strangers or copying artwork.

q.s: Compare how different objects preserve a music story.
st: Choose two displayed objects in an open gallery.
Read their labels and record each object’s stated connection to a person or event.
Notice one difference in the kinds of stories the objects tell.

packs.title: Lines along the Cumberland
packs.promise: Find a quieter pattern in downtown and the riverfront.

q.s: Find a route, an edge and a horizon.
st: From a clear upper path, find one line in the paving, one at the riverbank and one in the far view.
Describe how their directions differ; no descent to docks or steps is needed.
Save a three-part note or one view that shows your lines.

q.s: Look beyond the lights for building details.
st: Choose a clear sidewalk position; leave loud or crowded areas when needed.
Find three contrasting surfaces on outward-facing buildings, such as masonry, glass or metal.
Record the materials or describe their textures. No venue entry, drink or music performance is needed.

q.s: Find three details that help a shared path work.
st: Use only the open public greenway outside the concert gates.
Find a surface for moving, an edge that guides the route and a place where two materials meet.
Describe all three without stopping at a narrow crossing.
